full_judgment: 33. On critical analysis of the evidence on record it appears to us that the deceased Razia met the tragic end of her life while she was living with her accused husband Zakir in the same conjugal home. In view of such facts and circumstances of the case the husband i.e. the appellant Zakir Hossain is under obligation to explain such death in view of the provision laid down in section 106 of the Evidence Act. It is well settled that when it is established that the husband and wife were residing in the same house at the relevant time the husband is duty bound to explain the circumstances how his wife met with her death in his house and in absence of any explanation coming from the husband irresistible presumption is that it is the husband who is responsible for her death. With this regard reliance can be placed in the case of State vs Md Aynul Haq reported in 9 MLR 393. This view receives support in the cases of Gauranga Kumar Saha vs State reported in 2 BLC (AD) 126. Abdul Mutaleb Hawlader vs State reported in 5 MLR (AD) 362. State vs Safiqul Islam reported in 43 DLR (AD) 92, State vs Kalu Bepari reported in 43 DLR 249 and Dipok Kumar Saha vs State reported in 40 DLR 139.
